name: Buckshot Bourbon
tagline: Dust, steel strings, and a second chance at midnight.
description: A country-rock outfit that treats the open road like a studio. Buckshot Bourbon writes bar-room hymns with arena-sized choruses — whiskey-warm guitars, stacked harmonies, and stories that refuse to sand off their edges.
biography: Buckshot Bourbon started as a Friday-night residency in a converted feed mill north of the city. What began as three-hour sets for regulars became a catalog of songs about work, weather, loyalty, and the kind of love that leaves boot prints. Quantum Frequency Records signed the group after a live tape of 'Last Call Gravity' circulated through the label's A&R circle. They remain proudly analog in spirit — tracking live when it serves the song — while using the label as a launchpad to take country-rock somewhere less expected.

members.name: Cole Harlan
members.bio: Frontman and principal songwriter. Cole writes like he talks: plain, pointed, and a little dangerous after midnight.

members.name: Mae Riven
members.bio: The high harmony and the wild card. Mae's fiddle lines are the band's secret weapon.

members.name: Dutch Keller
members.bio: Keeps the floorboards moving. Dutch came up playing roadhouses from Buffalo to Birmingham.

members.name: Rex Lang
members.bio: A pocket drummer with a stomping right foot and a collection of vintage snares.

name: Sawyer Kennedy
tagline: Nashville steel with a late-night conscience.
description: A solo Nashville country artist who writes like a novelist and sings like the last person left in the room. Sawyer Kennedy's catalog is intimate, cinematic, and unafraid of silence.
biography: Sawyer Kennedy moved to Nashville with a notebook and a borrowed Telecaster. After two winters of writer's rounds and one very public breakup record, the songs started traveling further than the gigs. QFR heard a demo of 'Glass Off the Dashboard' and offered a home that would not force a radio template onto a storyteller. Sawyer records with a small rotating cast of Nashville players and produces with a documentary ear — room tone, breath, and the scrape of a chair are part of the arrangement.

members.name: Sawyer Kennedy
members.bio: Solo artist. Writes, sings, and produces from a converted garage studio east of downtown Nashville.

name: Fractal Hearts
tagline: Long-form rock for people who still look up.
description: Progressive, cosmic, and meticulously built. Fractal Hearts treat albums like constellations — motifs return, time signatures tilt, and guitars bloom into atmospheres.
biography: Fractal Hearts formed in a Portland rehearsal loft after a failed jazz-fusion project and a successful all-night planetarium shift. Their music folds math-rock discipline into space-rock wonder. QFR signed them for the ambition: records that reward headphones, stages that reward patience, and a visual language of recursive geometry. Live, they run a three-screen light plot designed by the drummer.

members.name: Nova Ellison
members.bio: Architect of the band's looping motifs and soaring mid-song key changes.

members.name: Iris Venn
members.bio: Builds the interstellar weather system the guitars fly through.

members.name: Kal Dreher
members.bio: A melodic bassist who treats odd meters like a conversation, not a stunt.

members.name: Jin Park
members.bio: Polyrhythmic engine and the designer of the live light fractal.

name: Grassroots Rebellion
description: Punk rock with pop-punk adrenaline and alt-rock craft. Grassroots Rebellion write two-minute arguments you can shout from a sticky floor.
biography: Grassroots Rebellion came up on basement bills, community radio, and a photocopied zine that outlived three practice spaces. Their songs are short, sharp, and surprisingly tender in the third verse. QFR wanted a band that could sit next to country and nu-metal without blinking — GR is that band. They still run their own merch table.

members.name: Tia Morales
members.bio: Lyricist of the uprising. Tia writes slogans that still feel like diary entries.

members.name: Benji Crowe
members.bio: Downstrokes, delay, and a gift for the one note that makes a chorus lift.

members.name: Pam Okoye
members.bio: The low-end argument. Pam's backing vocals are half the band's identity.

members.name: Otto Finch
members.bio: Fast, precise, and allergic to drum fills that last longer than the point.

name: Warpnotix
description: A DJ/producer building kinetic, nocturnal electronic music — warehouse pressure, neon melancholy, and drops engineered like architecture.
biography: Warpnotix (Wren Nox) spent a decade inside other people's tracks as a mix engineer before stepping in front of the decks. The Warpnotix project is a laboratory for dance-floor physics: sub that you feel in your ribs, breaks that reset the room, and a visual identity of warped grids. QFR signed Wren to prove the label's universe is not genre-bound. Club nights, festival afters, and headphone albums all sit in the same catalog.

members.name: Wren Nox
members.bio: The entire Warpnotix operation: writing, production, live sets, and visual direction.

name: Sound Shamans
description: Alt-rock built on hypnotic riffs, desert air, and a live reputation that borders on ceremony. Sound Shamans treat volume as a language.
biography: Sound Shamans emerged from Austin's late-night circuit with a reputation for sets that felt longer than the clock. They write in cycles and drones, then smash those cycles with choruses. The band's visual world is ochre, bone, and blue-black night. QFR brought them in to hold the indie/alt lane without turning it into a costume.

members.name: Rowan Hale
members.bio: Writes the incantations. A baritone that can go from whisper to weather.

members.name: Leah Voss
members.bio: Pedalboard cartographer. Leah's textures are half the band's atmosphere.

members.name: Mik Santos
members.bio: Holds the ritual down. Prefers one great note to twelve busy ones.

members.name: Ada Quinn
members.bio: Drives the trance. Ada's tom patterns are the band's pulse.

name: Immovable Giants
description: Chicago alt-rock that builds cathedrals out of patience. Immovable Giants write slow-burn anthems for people who stayed.
biography: Immovable Giants have been a Chicago secret for a decade: winter records, sold-out rooms, and a refusal to hurry. Their songs start small and become inevitable. QFR signed them to give the catalog a backbone of adult, unshowy rock — the kind that still hits like weather. The band records to tape when the song asks for it and to a laptop when it doesn't.

members.name: Ellen Marsh
members.bio: The still point. Ellen writes about endurance without making a speech of it.

members.name: Theo Brant
members.bio: Architect of the band's huge, patient chord voicings.

members.name: Nori Blake
members.bio: Melodic ballast. Nori's voice is the ghost in the choruses.

members.name: Cam Ruiz
members.bio: Dynamics first. Cam can make a verse feel like a held breath.

name: The Jones Beach Boys
tagline: Reverb, salt, and a perfect chorus.
description: A 1960s-surf-influenced group that treats the shoreline as a time machine. Twang, harmony, and summer even in January.
biography: The Jones Beach Boys started as a joke name and became a real band the night they learned four-part surf harmony in a parking lot. They write instrumentals and vocal tunes with equal love for spring reverb and unsarcastic joy. QFR signed them because the roster needed sun — and because the songs are better than nostalgia. They record live in a beach bungalow when the weather allows.

members.name: Nick Ellery
members.bio: Whammy-bar poet. Nick collects vintage Fenders the way other people collect postcards.

members.name: Sam Prieto
members.bio: The smile in the mix and the architect of the vocal stacks.

members.name: Dewey Hart
members.bio: Walking lines, spring-reverb grin, never in a hurry.

members.name: Kit Ambrose
members.bio: Ride-cymbal specialist. Kit plays like the tide coming in.

name: The Cosmic Run
tagline: Campfire songs for the upper atmosphere.
description: Alt-folk-rock that starts on a trail and ends in orbit. Acoustic bones, electric weather, and lyrics that look both inward and up.
biography: The Cosmic Run write on long drives and longer hikes. Their records move from fingerpicked confessionals to wide, night-sky rock without losing the plot. QFR heard them as the connective tissue of the roster — the band that makes country fans stay for the psych set. They self-produce with a mobile rig and a stubborn love of first takes.

members.name: June Calder
members.bio: The compass. June's songs are maps disguised as letters.

members.name: Eli Navarro
members.bio: Paints the sky around the acoustic bones.

members.name: Posey Lin
members.bio: Folk-root low end with a harmony sense from choir-kid years.

members.name: Hart Benson
members.bio: Brushes, boots, and the occasional thunder roll.

name: Moonflower Radio
tagline: Tune in. Drift. Come back changed.
description: Psychedelic alt-rock transmitted like a late-night station from another decade. Pedals, poetry, and patiently exploding choruses.
biography: Moonflower Radio have always sounded like a broadcast you found by accident and then never left. They came out of San Francisco's psych revival without becoming a museum act. QFR signed them for the color they add to the universe — washed-out film, analog delay, and lyrics that treat consciousness as a collaborative instrument. Their live shows are famously long and famously kind.

members.name: Lark Emerson
members.bio: Soft-loud mystic. Lark writes like a DJ of memories.

members.name: Suki Arden
members.bio: Organ, mellotron, and the voice that makes verses levitate.

members.name: Paulie Trent
members.bio: Hypnotic, patient, slightly behind the beat on purpose.

members.name: Dove Kim
members.bio: Plays time like it's elastic. A student of both motorik and swing.

name: Find/Replace
description: Industrial rock colliding with nu-metal weight. Find/Replace write about systems, glitches, and the people caught in the search field.
biography: Find/Replace formed in a Detroit warehouse that used to stamp auto parts. The building's acoustics — and its ghosts — are in the records. They sample factory ambience, scream like a UI error, and still write choruses you can put a fist in the air for. QFR wanted industrial muscle without corporate dystopia-as-cosplay. Find/Replace is the real weather of a city that makes things.

members.name: Hex Calder
members.bio: Half preacher, half compiler error. Hex writes in all-caps feelings.

members.name: Vex Moreau
members.bio: Seven-string architect. Treats feedback as a lead instrument.

members.name: Null Reyes
members.bio: The industrial floor. Null's tone is a building settling.

members.name: Tick Abram
members.bio: Acoustic kit triggered into a machine. Human swing, factory precision.

name: Immortal Prophets
description: Nu-metal with a philosophical streak. Immortal Prophets write about fate, fury, and the joke of being mortal at this volume.
biography: Immortal Prophets came out of Cleveland's heavy circuit with riffs that felt both vintage-2000 and unnervingly current. They rap, they scream, they stack gang vocals, and they mean it. QFR signed them to hold the heavy lane with dignity — no nostalgia trap, no irony shield. The band's mythos is self-made: sigils, sermons, and a live show that feels like a rite.

members.name: Cain Vesper
members.bio: The prophet. Moves from whisper to rupture without a seam.

members.name: Joss Halek
members.bio: Drop-tuned author of the band's central riffs.

members.name: Mira Solt
members.bio: The low sermon. Mira's tone is half the prophecy.

members.name: Rook Danner
members.bio: Double-kick philosopher. Rook writes beats like arguments.

name: Firewall Nation
description: Nu-metal colliding with rap-rock cadence. Firewall Nation write about networks, loyalty, and what gets through.
biography: Firewall Nation started as a cypher that needed guitars. Atlanta's rap precision met Midwestern heaviness after a tour van accident (minor, mythologized) put a producer and a metal guitarist in the same waiting room. The result is a band that can cut a verse like a verse and a chorus like a wall. QFR signed them as proof that the roster's 'nation' is bigger than any one scene.

members.name: Ace Calderon
members.bio: The packet. Ace writes in couplets that hit like exploits.

members.name: Rye Patton
members.bio: The payload. Rye turns choruses into sirens.

members.name: Gio Hart
members.bio: Djent-adjacent without the lecture. Gio loves a dirty octave.

members.name: Zee Okonkwo
members.bio: 808s under a live bass. Zee produces the band's records in-house.

members.name: Pix Renner
members.bio: Trap hats meet live kit. Pix is the reason the drop lands.
